newsitem.title: HAITI: Students, police clash in Port-au-Prince.
newsitem.headline: Students, police clash in Port-au-Prince.

text.p: Police clashed with students who occupied a school in the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince on Thursday and several people were wounded, including a boy shot in the head, witnesses said.
Police fired tear gas and bullets. At least two other protesters received bullet wounds and several were beaten, the witnesses said.

Rioting spread to downtown streets and demonstrators set fire to cars, torched a courthouse and hurled rocks through shop windows. Several houses also caught fire, forcing residents to flee with the few belongings they could grab, and business owners closed shops as the unrest grew.
The fate of the boy who was shot in the head was not known but he appeared to be alive as students ran through the streets with him. Police later took him to a hospital.
The Petion School, which was occupied by the students, has been closed since Monday when teachers walked out, saying they had not been paid for months.

Discontent has been rife among Haiti's poor over a government privatisation plan and austerity measures promoted by the International Monetary Fund in what is already the poorest country in the Americas.
